overview.label: 02 / The overview
overview.title: The idea isn't the bottleneck. Everything around it is.
overview.body: Good scenario design is slow, and the idea is rarely the hard part. The time goes to everything around it: turning lived experience into clear behaviors, drafting branches, making dozens of consistent images, catching mismatches across screens, and keeping the case study up to date. Done by hand, that work crowds out the judgment calls that decide whether a scenario actually lands for a learner.

pipeline.label: 03 / The pipeline
pipeline.title: A repeatable pipeline, not one prompt at a time.
pipeline.body: Instead of asking AI one question at a time, I run every project through the same stages. Each stage hands its output to the next, and I make the call at every gate.
pipeline.quote: AI does the legwork. I make the calls.

practice.label: 04 / In practice
practice.title: Where the pipeline shows up in real work.
items: AI image pipeline
I set the look in Midjourney, then generate scenes in Flora AI with Nano Banana, keeping the same players, uniforms and gym consistent across all three sets of Coaching Through Conflict.
Action maps & storyboards
Claude helps me draft action maps and storyboard tables from my own experience. I decide which behaviors matter and what every screen says.
One design, any platform
The same script and images move from a Figma prototype to a web build to Articulate Storyline 360, so the module can run wherever learners are.
Branching prototypes in Figma
68 connected screens with prototype links, variables that remember a learner's guess, overlays and Smart Animate.
Vibe-coded builds
Pip's Number Garden, the TV Wall Sales Simulator and this website were built by describing what I wanted and refining the code with AI.
Morning roundup
A scheduled task searches new learning design roles every weekday morning and sends me the best matches before I start my day.

rules.label: 05 / The rules
rules.title: Six rules I hold every project to.
items: No invented numbers
Every claim is checked against my real facts. If I haven't measured it, it doesn't go on the page.
Nothing ships without a playthrough
I walk every branch as a learner would before calling a module done, and fix what feels off.
Real people stay protected
Jersey numbers stand in for student-athletes, AI scenes use no real faces from my teams, and images carry no brand logos.
Every module gets an evaluation plan
Each project names what success looks like at all four Kirkpatrick levels before I call it done.
The style guide is the standard
Colors, type, buttons and spacing come from one style guide, so every screen matches without guesswork.
Accessibility is part of done
Readable sizes, alt text and a reduced-motion setting are built in from the start, not added at the end.

principle.label: 06 / The principle
principle.title: I own the judgment calls.
principle.body: AI doesn't decide what's true, what's fair to a learner, or how a moment should feel. It speeds up the busywork so I can spend my time on the parts only a designer should own. I'm open about where AI helps, because being clear about that line is part of designing responsibly.

why.label: 07 / Why it matters
why.title: The question every hiring team is asking.
why.body: Hiring teams keep asking how people actually use AI in learning design, beyond a chatbot. This is my answer in practice: every project and visual on this site came out of this pipeline.
